title: What Happens When You Blush?
sources: Cleveland Clinic, 'Skin Flushing' (skin flushing, or blushing, is the sudden increase of blood flow to your cheeks, neck or upper chest; it causes your cheeks, neck or upper chest to turn red or darker temporarily; on a dark skin tone it can cause the skin on these parts to darken slightly; most often blushing is a reaction to strong emotions like affection or embarrassment; increased blood flow to your head, face, neck or upper chest causes flushed skin; if a strong emotion is the culprit, symptoms may go away once you relax): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/symptoms/skin-flushing

Better Health Channel (Victoria State Government, Department of Health), 'Blushing and flushing', reviewed 2023-10-12 (facial blushing is an involuntary reddening of the face due to embarrassment or stress; given the right stimulus such as embarrassment, the nerves prompt the blood vessels to open wide, flooding the skin with blood; the sympathetic nervous system regulates glands and organs without our conscious effort; in some people the ears, neck and chest also blush): https://www.betterhealth.vic.gov.au/health/conditionsandtreatments/blushing-and-flushing

Tease (next video): Cleveland Clinic, 'Motion Sickness' (happens when your eyes, inner ear and body send conflicting messages to your brain; symptoms can come on gradually or suddenly and include nausea, dizziness, headache, a cold sweat and excess saliva): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/12782-motion-sickness

lines.text: Blushing can hit three places, and one hides under your shirt.

lines.text: It starts with a strong feeling, like embarrassment or affection.

lines.text: Your nerves tell the blood vessels in your face to open wide,

lines.text: flooding the skin with blood, no permission needed.

In some people, the blood rush keeps going,
down the neck and right onto the upper chest.

lines.text: Once you relax, it usually fades on its own.
